source: .github/workflows/nodejs.yml, job `test-runtime-vm-modules`, transcribed by reading the repository
constructedIndependently: Written by reading the workflow file. The inference engine was not consulted and this file is not generated from any ExecutionGraph.
cellSelection: The job hard-codes runs-on: ubuntu-latest and matrices node-version [18.x, 20.x, 22.x, 24.x, 25.x, 26.x]. 22.x is the single in-environment cell; the other five are OUT_OF_ENVIRONMENT, recorded and not executed.

substitutions.${CPU_CORES}: Resolved by the harness to the container's own core count, and recorded in the step receipt. CI obtains this value from `SimenB/github-actions-cpu-cores`, a third-party action whose sole documented function is to report the runner's CPU count; the workflow itself does not state a number. Substituting it is a faithful transcription of the semantics, NOT command repair - but it is a licence the inference engine does not have, which is why docs/ci-reproduction-sample-01-amendment-1.md grades a refusal citing `steps.cpu-cores.outputs.count` as CORRECT_REFUSAL rather than counting it against DiffCI.

structuralNote: The test command is NOT a `run:` line. It is a string argument passed under `with:` to the third-party action `nick-fields/retry`, which executes it with up to 3 attempts and a 10-minute per-attempt timeout. The reference arm runs the command ONCE, directly: retry-on-error is a flake-tolerance policy, and repeating a failed suite would make the reference arm's result depend on how many times it was allowed to try.
conditionsApplied: The `map coverage` and `codecov` steps carry `if: always()` and follow the test step; they are not part of the TEST path and are excluded. No step in the path up to and including the suite is condition-skipped.

steps.evidence: REQUIRED BY THE ENVIRONMENT, not by the workflow. CI's actions/setup-node provisions yarn; the canonical container ships npm only. `yarn --immutable` is a Yarn Berry invocation and cannot run without it. Recorded here explicitly rather than hidden, and it is NOT a repair of a repository command - it is the container standing in for setup-node.

.github/workflows/nodejs.yml - `run jest-runtime tests with --experimental-vm-modules` -> `uses: nick-fields/retry` with `command: yarn jest-runtime-vm-modules-ci --max-workers ${{ steps.cpu-cores.outputs.count }}`
